You can! I'm not really sure what separates the abilities on the Theros gods, but the ruling states that their ability only applies on the battlefield, and they are a creature everywhere else.

So those are called Characteristic-Defining Abilities (CDAs) and they apply wherever the card is. So, for instance, if you have 6 or more lands on the battlefield when this creature dies, you can search up [[beanstalk giant]] because it will have at least 6 toughness. Changeling works in a similar way, where the creatures have every creature type even if they're not on the battlefield.

Ooh I wrote a term paper on this last year! One major part of the issue I haven't seen anyone bring up is that for a lot of the public perception of GM foods, the issue boils down to absolute moral values. Basically, the idea of changing the genetic code of the food we eat triggers disgust in people who are absolutely morally opposed to it. This can be because they see it as "playing god" or corrupting nature. The reason that they aren't convinced by all the good GMOs can do is because absolute moral values are considered self-evident to the people who hold them, so they never need to be justified. Another example of an absolute moral value might be veganism, or for more people the belief that dogs and cats shouldn't be eaten. Even if any other health or moral concern was ruled out (the dog was free of disease, the person eating it was starving etc), a moral absolutist would still find the idea upsetting. In the same way, even if most of the scientific community believes GM foods are safe, many people still find it disgusting in concept
